subject: Taxes
title: Taxing the Digital Economy
description: A quick, practical guide to Taxing the Digital Economy.

hook.text: Facebook earns $2 per user in India each quarter but pays almost no Indian tax.

buildup.text: Traditional tax requires a physical 'permanent establishment'—a factory, office, or store.

discovery.text: Pillar One would reallocate taxing rights to countries where customers are—not just where headquarters sit.

twist.text: Implementation stalled for years. Countries imposed unilateral digital taxes.

climax.text: Taxing the digital economy requires rewriting rules designed for physical goods.

punchline.text: $2 per user, zero tax in that country. The digital tax gap is massive.

quiz.question: Why is taxing digital companies so difficult?
options: Tax rules were designed for physical businesses with local presence
Digital companies are tax-exempt by law
